mainTopic: Can food that is אסור בהנאה (forbidden to benefit from) become impure as food (טומאת אוכלין)? The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון, and how it applies to a מנחה that became פיגול.
overview: A ברייתא lists foods that are forbidden even for benefit and asks whether they can still get טומאת אוכלין, the impurity that food receives. The תנא קמא says yes. רבי שמעון says no, except for בשר בחלב, which was once fit to eat (שעת הכושר). רבי יוחנן explains רבי שמעון's source: only food you may give to others counts as food. רבי אושעיא applies this to a מנחה that became פיגול, saying it gets no טומאת אוכלין. The גמרא challenges him from a ברייתא where רבי שמעון rules that a פיגול מנחה does get it. The answer is that it depends on whether the flour was ever fit, for example wheat made holy while still growing never was. The גמרא then asks whether the owner's ability to redeem the flour, or a מצוה to sprinkle blood, counts as if it already happened. It works this out through the cases of the פרה אדומה and meat left overnight before sprinkling. The amud ends by opening a new challenge from animal offerings made פיגול, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Forbidden foods still get food impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list: שור הנסקל, עגלה ערופה, צפורי מצורע, פטר חמור, and בשר בחלב all get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox that is stoned, a heifer whose neck is broken, the birds of a leper, a firstborn donkey, and meat cooked with milk all become impure with the impurity of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a list of foods that are forbidden, and says that all of them can still become impure as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item here is אסור בהנאה, so you may not eat it or get any benefit from it. Even so, this first opinion holds that it is still 'food' for the laws of טומאה. Being forbidden does not take away its status as food.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox stoned for killing a person; its meat is forbidden
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found
The birds used in the purification of a מצורע
A firstborn donkey (here, one whose neck was broken)
Meat cooked together with milk
The kind of impurity that food can receive

phrases.english: And an ox that is stoned, and a heifer whose neck is broken,
and the birds of a leper, and a firstborn donkey,
and meat cooked with milk,
all of them become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list from earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foods that are אסור בהנאה can still receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: רבי שמעון disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says none of these items get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: None of them become impure with the impurity of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion. He says none of these forbidden items can become impure as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, something you may not benefit from does not count as 'food' for טומאה. The two opinions disagree about whether a ban on benefit takes away an item's food status.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not become impure
A prohibition on getting any benefit from an item

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
None of them become impure with the impurity of food,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against the תנא קמא in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that are אסור בהנאה do not receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees about meat and milk
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees that בשר בחלב does get טומאת אוכלין, because it was once fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון agrees about meat cooked with milk that it becomes impure with the impurity of food, since it had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון makes one exception to his own rule: בשר בחלב can become impure as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before they were cooked together, the meat and the milk were each allowed and fit to eat. Because it once had food status (שעת הכושר), that status stays with it even after it became forbidden. The other items on the list were never fit as food in this way.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (on this point)
Since, because
A time when it was fit and allowed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: forbidden-to-benefit items are not 'food' for טומאה, unless they once had a שעת הכושר, as בשר בחלב did.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon agrees about meat cooked with milk
that it becomes impure with the impurity of food,
since it had a time when it was fit.
phrases.notes: He means that before the meat and milk were cooked together, each one was allowed to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי שמעון's rule from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בשר בחלב receives טומאת אוכלין even for רבי שמעון, because of its שעת הכושר.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains רבי שמעון's source: the פסוק 'food which may be eaten' teaches that only food you may give to others counts as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said that רבי יוחנן said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון? 'Of all food which may be eaten.' Food that you may feed to others is called food. Food that you may not feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן, quoted by רב אסי, asks why רבי שמעון holds his view and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק adds the words 'which may be eaten' to the word 'food'. רבי יוחנן reads this to mean food that is allowed to be eaten by others. Something that is אסור בהנאה may not be given to anyone, so it is not 'food' for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Which may be eaten
To feed it to others
Is called 'food'

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the rule we will use next: whether you may give an item to others decides whether it counts as food for טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
'Of all food which may be eaten.'
Food that you are able to feed to others
phrases.notes: 'Others' here means non-Jews. Even food a Jew may not eat could be given to them, unless benefit from it is forbidden.

phrases.english: is called food;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: food that you are not able to feed to others
is not called food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי שמעון's view from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only food that may be given to others counts as food for טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Applying the rule to a פיגול מנחה
steps.stepSummary: A מנחה that was made פיגול also may not be given to others, so for רבי שמעון it does not get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this one who made a meal offering פיגול too: it is food that you are not able to feed to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא takes רבי יוחנן's rule and applies it to the case being discussed: a מנחה that became פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one may benefit from a פיגול מנחה, so you cannot give it to others either. According to the פסוק's test, it is not 'food'. That is why, for רבי שמעון, it does not receive טומאת אוכלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Made an offering פיגול through a wrong intention about the time it would be eaten or burned
A meal offering
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a פיגול מנחה is not food for טומאה, because it may not be given to others.

phrases.english: And this one who made a meal offering פיגול, too,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים הוּא.
phrases.english: is food that you are not able to feed to others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 4 to the פיגול מנחה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because a פיגול מנחה may not be given to others, רבי שמעון holds it does not receive טומאת אוכלין. (The גמרא will soon challenge and limit this to a מנחה that never had a שעת הכושר.)

steps.title: Why not use the 'give to others' reason for meat in milk?
steps.stepSummary: If food that can be given to others counts as food, then בשר בחלב should qualify for that reason too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also get that meat cooked in milk is food for this reason: it is food you can feed to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the ברייתא. It just learned the rule 'food you may give to others is food,' and says that rule should also explain בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבי שמעון said בשר בחלב gets טומאת אוכלין because it was once fit to eat. But by the rule from step 4, there seems to be an easier reason: you may give בשר בחלב to others. So why did the ברייתא use the 'once fit' reason?

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true
Let him get it from: why not learn it from this simpler reason?
To feed it to others

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק in step 4 is right.

phrases.english: for meat in milk too, let him get it from the fact
that it is food that you are able
to feed to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 4 to question the reason given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in step 3 ('it was once fit') for why בשר בחלב gets טומאת אוכלין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's rule should already cover בשר בחלב, since you may give it to others. So why give a different reason?

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון allows benefit from meat in milk
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון holds בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit, so it may be given to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: Meat in milk is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit. The פסוק says 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God; do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.' Elsewhere it says 'You shall be holy men to Me, and do not eat flesh torn in the field.' Just as there it is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit, so too here it is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question. It brings a ברייתא proving that רבי שמעון allows benefit from בשר בחלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'holy' (קדוש / קדש). So רבי שמעון compares בשר בחלב to טרפה. Since טרפה is forbidden only to eat, בשר בחלב is also forbidden only to eat, and you may sell it or give it to a non-Jew. This proves that the question in step 6 is a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to eat
Allowed for benefit, like selling it or giving it away
An animal with a deadly injury or defect, which may not be eaten
Just as there, so too here: comparing two cases because the פסוקים share wording

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source that, for רבי שמעון, בשר בחלב is not forbidden for benefit. That is exactly why it counts as 'food you may give to others.'

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
meat in milk is forbidden to eat
but allowed for benefit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
phrases.english: as it says: 'For you are a holy people to ה׳ your God;
do not cook a kid in its mother's milk,'
and elsewhere it says:
'You shall be holy men to Me,
and flesh torn in the field you shall not eat.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה,
phrases.english: Just as there, it is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the טרפה in the second פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.english: so too here, it is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the question in step 6 by showing רבי שמעון allows benefit from בשר בחלב.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי שמעון, בשר בחלב is allowed for benefit and so may be given to others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון, comparing בשר בחלב to טרפה because both פסוקים say 'holy.'

steps.title: The ברייתא gives two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is giving one reason and adding another: meat in milk may be given to others, and it was also once fit even for a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and adding another. First: it is food that you can feed to others. And also: even for him, it had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי שמעון agrees with the 'give to others' reason, and he adds a second reason on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is רבי יוחנן's rule: it may be given to others. Reason two goes further: even for the Jew himself, the meat and the milk were each fine to eat before they were cooked together. The ברייתא in step 3 mentioned the second reason, but that does not mean it rejects the first.

keyTerms.meaning: He says one reason and adds another
For him himself, meaning the Jew who owns it
A time when it was fit, here meaning fit to eat

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, בשר בחלב gets טומאת אוכלין for two reasons: you may give it to others, and it was once fit to eat even for a Jew.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא in step 3 named only the 'once fit' reason. That does not mean the 'give to others' reason fails here. The second reason is simply added on top of the first.

phrases.english: He is saying one thing, and another:
One: that it is food that you are able
to feed to others,
and another: even for him himself
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the Jew who owns it, not the others he could give it to.

phrases.english: it had a time when it was fit.
phrases.notes: Before they were cooked together, the meat and the milk were each fine to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 6–7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reasons are true; the ברייתא added a further reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא used only 'it was once fit,' it seemed that the 'give to others' reason did not apply to בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both reasons apply. The 'once fit' reason is an extra point, saying that even for the owner himself it was once food.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בשר בחלב gets טומאת אוכלין for רבי שמעון for two reasons at once.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי שמעון's ruling on נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge from a ברייתא where רבי שמעון says some נותר gets טומאת אוכלין and some does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, some נותר makes things impure with food impurity, and some נותר does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge to the ruling it just reached. This line only sets up the source; the actual problem will come in the next lines of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening about נותר is background. רבי שמעון ties food status to whether the item was ever fit to eat, which explains why some נותר gets טומאת אוכלין and some does not. The real problem comes at the end of this ברייתא (step 11), which rules on a פיגול מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of a קרבן left past the time it may be eaten
Can become impure with food impurity and pass it on

phrases.english: They raised a challenge:
Rabbi Shimon says,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ נוֹתָר שֶׁהוּא מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין,
phrases.english: there is נותר that becomes impure with food impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ נוֹתָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין.
phrases.english: and there is נותר that does not become impure with food impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, יֵשׁ נוֹתָר שֶׁהוּא מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ruling of step 5 and opens a new challenge to it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 5 that, for רבי שמעון, a forbidden קרבן item like פיגול does not get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא of רבי שמעון goes on to rule that a פיגול מנחה does get טומאת אוכלין (step 11). That contradicts step 5.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains which נותר gets food impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that meat left overnight before the זריקה gets no טומאת אוכלין, but meat left overnight after the זריקה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If it was left overnight before the blood was sprinkled, it does not get food impurity. If it was left overnight after the sprinkling, it does get food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the ברייתא it started in step 9. Here the ברייתא explains when נותר gets טומאת אוכלין and when it does not. This is still setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the זריקה the meat was never allowed to be eaten, so it never counted as food. After the זריקה there was a window when it could be eaten, so it counts as food even after it becomes נותר. The key factor is whether the meat was ever fit to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Was left overnight, which turns sacrificial meat into נותר
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, which permits the meat to be eaten
The kind of impurity that applies to food

phrases.english: How so?
If it was left overnight before the sprinkling –
it is not susceptible to food impurity,
phrases.notes: Before the sprinkling, the meat was never allowed to be eaten.

phrases.english: after the sprinkling –
it is susceptible to food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 9 by explaining which נותר gets טומאת אוכלין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נותר gets טומאת אוכלין only if it was left overnight after the זריקה, once it had been fit to eat.

steps.title: The ברייתא says a פיגול מנחה does get food impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says animal offerings that became פיגול get no טומאת אוכלין, but a מנחה that became פיגול does. This contradicts step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: And פיגול, whether in קדשי קדשים or in קדשים קלים, does not get food impurity. If someone made a מנחה פיגול, it does get food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a ruling about a מנחה that became פיגול. This is the point of the challenge, because it clashes with what was said earlier about רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that for רבי שמעון a פיגול מנחה does not get טומאת אוכלין, because it may not be given to others. Here the ברייתא of רבי שמעון says it does get טומאת אוכלין. So the two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten or offered
Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of a lower level of holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The animal offerings and the מנחה get opposite rulings here. An animal that became פיגול was never fit to eat, but the flour of a מנחה usually was fit before it was made holy.

phrases.english: And פיגול,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'but isn't it'; the corrected wording leaves it out and just says 'and פיגול'.

phrases.english: whether in offerings of the most holy level
or in offerings of lower holiness –
it is not susceptible to food impurity.
If he made a meal offering פיגול –
it is susceptible to food impurity.
phrases.notes: This clashes with step 5, which said a פיגול מנחה gets no food impurity for רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and brings out the ruling that creates the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 5 that, for רבי שמעון, a פיגול מנחה does not get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון rules directly that a פיגול מנחה does get טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: It depends on whether the מנחה was ever fit
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: the ברייתא speaks of a מנחה that had a שעת הכושר, and step 5 speaks of one that never did.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it had a time when it was fit, and there it did not have a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two rulings deal with two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flour was once fit to eat before it became holy, it counts as food and gets טומאת אוכלין even after it becomes פיגול. If it never had such a moment, it never counted as food. So both rulings stand, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, meaning there is no contradiction
A time when something was fit, here fit to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the same idea the ברייתא used for נותר in step 10. Something that was once fit to eat keeps the status of food.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
here – where it had a time of being fit,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא, which says it does get food impurity.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן – שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: there – where it did not have a time of being fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן – שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings about a פיגול מנחה seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מנחה that once had a שעת הכושר gets טומאת אוכלין. One that never had such a time does not.

steps.title: How could a מנחה never have been fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case could leave a מנחה with no time of being fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case where it did not have a time of being fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real example of the second case. Flour normally seems fit to eat before it becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary wheat or flour can be eaten before it is set aside as a מנחה. So it is hard to picture a מנחה that never had a שעת הכושר. The גמרא needs a concrete case to make the answer work.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? A request for a concrete case

phrases.english: What are the circumstances
where it did not have a time of being fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי דְּלֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a real example of the case the answer in step 12 relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where a מנחה never had a שעת הכושר.

steps.title: The wheat was made holy while still growing
steps.stepSummary: The case is when the wheat was made holy while still attached to the ground, so it was never fit as ordinary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he made them holy while they were still attached to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case: someone made the wheat holy while it was still growing in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While still attached to the ground, the wheat could not yet get טומאה as food. By the time it was cut, it was already holy and forbidden as ordinary food. So it never had a שעת הכושר, and if it becomes פיגול it gets no טומאת אוכלין.

keyTerms.meaning: He made them holy (consecrated them)
Attached to the ground, still growing

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, what counts is whether the item was ever fit to eat (שעת הכושר). A פיגול מנחה gets טומאת אוכלין if it once was fit. It does not if it never was, such as wheat made holy while still growing.

phrases.english: Where he consecrated them
while attached to the ground.
phrases.notes: Growing produce cannot yet become impure as food, and once it was cut it was already holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a concrete case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wheat was made holy while still attached to the ground, so it was never fit as food.

steps.title: Why not redeem the flour and give it a time of being fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 14: the owner could redeem the flour, so it could have become ordinary food. This works under the version of רבי אושעיא that even pure meal offerings can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him redeem them! This is fine according to the version where רבי אושעיא said: impure ones are redeemed, pure ones are not. But according to the version that says even pure ones are redeemed, let him redeem them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 14. Even wheat made holy in the ground could be redeemed and become ordinary food, so it would have a שעת הכושר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming moves the holiness onto money, and the flour becomes חולין, fit for anyone to eat. Under the version where only impure meal offerings can be redeemed, pure flour could never become food, so step 14 works. Under the version where even pure ones can be redeemed, the flour always had a path to being food, and the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him redeem them, meaning move their holiness onto money so they become ordinary
This works out well (used to set up 'but according to the other view...')
Version or wording of a statement
Impure ones / pure ones
Fine, it works well

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי אושעיא holds two opinions. These are two different reports of what he said, and the challenge only works against one of them.

phrases.english: But let him redeem them!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the flour from step 14. Once redeemed it becomes ordinary food, so it would have a time of being fit to eat.

phrases.english: This works out well according to this version
in which Rabbi Oshaya said:
Impure ones are redeemed,
phrases.notes: He is talking about meal offerings and libations that were not yet put into a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: pure ones are not redeemed. That is fine.
But according to this version, which says,
even pure ones are redeemed,
let him redeem them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 14 as an example of a מנחה with no שעת הכושר.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14's claim that wheat made holy while attached never had a time of being fit to eat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even pure flour can be redeemed, the owner always had the option to make it ordinary food, so it did have a potential שעת הכושר.

steps.title: He has not actually redeemed it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whatever he could do, right now he has not redeemed it, so it still has no time of being fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, right now he has not redeemed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 14. What counts is what really happened, and the flour was never actually redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates being able to redeem from actually redeeming. A שעת הכושר depends on the flour truly being fit, not on an option the owner never used.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, right now
He has not redeemed it

phrases.english: In any event, right now he has not redeemed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Actual reality versus possibility: an option that was not used does not count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he could redeem it, the flour should count as having a time of being fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was never actually redeemed, so it never had a real time of being fit to eat.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון says what can be redeemed counts as redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 16 using רבי שמעון's rule: anything standing to be redeemed is treated as already redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since, if he wants, he can redeem it, we have heard that רבי שמעון says: anything that stands to be redeemed is considered as if it were redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 16. רבי שמעון holds that having the ability to redeem is as good as redeeming, so the flour should count as ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said only actual redemption counts. רבי שמעון's rule says the opposite: if something is set to be redeemed, we treat it as already redeemed. If that rule applies here, the flour did have a שעת הכושר, and step 16's answer falls apart. Step 18 gives the source for this rule, and step 19 answers the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wants
We have heard that he holds
Anything that stands to be redeemed is treated as already redeemed

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule כׇּל הָעוֹמֵד לִפְדּוֹת כְּפָדוּי דָּמֵי is a well-known principle: something about to happen can be treated as if it already happened.

phrases.english: But since, if he wants, he can redeem it,
we have heard that Rabbi Shimon says:
anything that stands to be redeemed is considered as if it were redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that only actual redemption counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי שמעון's principle, the ability to redeem is treated as redemption, so the flour should count as ordinary food with a שעת הכושר.

steps.title: The source: רבי שמעון on the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the rule from step 17. רבי שמעון says a פרה אדומה can get food impurity because it had a time of being fit. ריש לקיש explains that רבי שמעון holds the פרה can be redeemed even on its pyre.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says a red heifer can become impure with food impurity, since it had a time of being fit. And ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון used to say that a red heifer can be redeemed even when it is already on its pyre.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing where the rule in step 17 comes from. It points to רבי שמעון's teaching about the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a פרה אדומה is slaughtered, no one may use or eat it, so how could it ever have been 'food'? ריש לקיש explains that רבי שמעון holds it can always be redeemed, even on the pyre, so it is treated as if already redeemed and fit to eat. The challenge to step 16 follows: a מנחה that can be redeemed should also count as fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify people
The kind of impurity that only food can receive
A time when something was fit, here meaning fit to be eaten
The pyre where the פרה is burned

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
A red heifer can become impure with the impurity of food,
since it had a time of being fit.
And Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Shimon used to say,
a red heifer can be redeemed even on top of its pyre.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule used in step 17's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that anything standing to be redeemed is treated as already redeemed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון about פרה אדומה and food impurity, as explained by ריש לקיש

steps.title: A פרה stands to be redeemed, but a מנחה does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. A פרה counts as standing to be redeemed because there is a מצוה to redeem it if a nicer one is found. There is no such מצוה for מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? It makes sense for a פרה, which stands to be redeemed, because if he finds another one nicer than it, it is a מצוה to redeem it. But these מנחות, is there a מצוה to redeem them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of steps 17-18 by showing the פרה case is different from a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to redeem something is not enough. A פרה is 'standing to be redeemed' because there is a real מצוה to swap it for a better one. With a מנחה there is no מצוה to redeem it, so we cannot treat it as already redeemed, and step 16's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are different)
It makes sense with regard to...
Standing to be redeemed, expected to be redeemed
Nicer, better than it

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
It makes sense with a red heifer: it stands to be redeemed,
since if he found another one nicer than it,
it is a מצוה to redeem it.
But these meal offerings, is it a מצוה to redeem them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 17-18 by splitting the פרה case from the מנחה case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything that could be redeemed is treated as already redeemed, so a מנחה also had a time of being fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something with a מצוה to redeem it counts as 'standing to be redeemed'; a מנחה has no such מצוה.

steps.title: Challenge from meat left overnight before sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 19. With meat left overnight before the blood was sprinkled, there was a מצוה to sprinkle and he could have done it, yet רבי שמעון teaches it does not get food impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about meat that was left overnight before the sprinkling of the blood? There was a מצוה to sprinkle it, and if he wanted he could have sprinkled it. Yet it teaches that it does not get food impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the distinction of step 19 by bringing a case where there was a מצוה, and still it was not treated as fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of a קרבן becomes fit to eat only after the blood is sprinkled. Here there was a מצוה to sprinkle and he could have done so, so by step 19's logic the meat should count as if already sprinkled. Yet רבי שמעון rules it cannot get food impurity, so having a מצוה seems not to be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Was left overnight (and so became disqualified)
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח
If he wanted (he was able to)

phrases.english: But what about meat left overnight before the sprinkling,
where it was a מצוה to sprinkle it,
and if he had wanted, he could have sprinkled,
and yet it teaches that it does not get the impurity of food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 19's claim that a מצוה to act makes something count as already done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of meat left overnight before sprinkling there was a מצוה and ability to sprinkle, yet רבי שמעון does not treat it as fit food.

steps.title: There was no time left in the day to sprinkle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks of a case where there was not enough time left in the day to sprinkle the blood, so it never stood to be sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where there was not enough time left in the day to sprinkle it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 20 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal was slaughtered right before sunset, there was never a real chance to sprinkle that day. So the blood never 'stood to be sprinkled' and the meat never had a time of being fit. The distinction of step 19 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (narrowing the case)
Enough time left in the day

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, something counts as 'standing' to be redeemed or sprinkled only if there is a real מצוה and a real chance to do it. A פרה qualifies; a מנחה does not, and blood with no time left in the day does not either.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where there was not enough time left in the day to sprinkle it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat left overnight had a real chance to be sprinkled, so it should count as fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is when there was no time left that day, so the blood never stood to be sprinkled.

steps.title: What if there was time left in the day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law would be if there WAS time in the day to sprinkle the blood. It assumes the meat would then get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there was time left in the day to sprinkle, what would the law be? Then the meat would get food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא follows up on step 21 by asking about the opposite case, when there was time left in the day. It assumes the meat would then get food impurity, and this sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 limited the ברייתא to a case with no time left to sprinkle. That implies a different result when there was time: the meat 'stood to be sprinkled', so it counts as fit and can get טומאת אוכלין. The גמרא states this result so it can test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough time left in the day (here, to sprinkle the blood before nightfall)
The kind of impurity that food can receive
What? (what is the law?)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁהוּת בְּיוֹם, מַאי?
phrases.english: But if there was time for it in the day, what?
phrases.notes: He means there was still enough daylight after the שחיטה to sprinkle the blood.

phrases.english: It is susceptible to the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁהוּת בְּיוֹם, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 21's answer implies for the opposite case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for meat left overnight when there was time in the day to sprinkle the blood.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It would be susceptible to טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Why not split the case itself?
steps.stepSummary: If time in the day makes a difference, רבי שמעון should have made the split inside the 'before sprinkling' case itself, instead of contrasting before and after sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of teaching that meat left overnight after sprinkling gets food impurity, he should have split the first case itself: When is this said? When there was no time in the day. But if there was time in the day, it does get food impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 21. If time in the day matters, why didn't the ברייתא state that split directly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasted 'left overnight before sprinkling' with 'left overnight after sprinkling.' If step 21 is right, a more useful teaching would split the 'before sprinkling' case into no time versus time. Since the ברייתא did not seem to do this, maybe step 21's answer is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather than teaching
Let him make the split within the same case
In what case is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather than teaching: left overnight after sprinkling
phrases.notes: Here לָן means 'stayed overnight.' It is not the word 'to us.'

phrases.english: it is susceptible to the impurity of food –
let him distinguish within that case itself:
In what case are these words said?
Where there was no time for it in the day,
but if there was time for it in the day –
it is susceptible to the impurity of food!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי לָן לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין לִיפְלוֹג בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result stated in step 22 to attack the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 21 that the ברייתא speaks of a case with no time left in the day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If time in the day changes the law, the ברייתא should have taught that split directly instead of contrasting before and after sprinkling.

steps.title: That is exactly what he meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does teach this split. 'Before' and 'after' mean before or after the meat became fit for sprinkling, not before or after the actual sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying: if it was left overnight before it became fit for sprinkling, it does not get food impurity. If it was left overnight after it became fit for sprinkling, it does get food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently. 'After sprinkling' really means 'after it became fit to be sprinkled.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the words are understood this way, the ברייתא already contains the split the challenge asked for. 'Before it was fit for sprinkling' means there was no time left in the day. 'After it was fit' means there was time, even if nobody actually sprinkled. So the answer of step 21 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what he is saying
That it becomes fit (available) for sprinkling
Was left overnight (and became disqualified)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading of רבי שמעון, meat that could have had its blood sprinkled that day counts as fit, so it can get טומאת אוכלין even if the blood was never sprinkled.

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying:
If it was left overnight before it was fit for sprinkling –
it is not susceptible to the impurity of food,
after it was fit for sprinkling –
it is susceptible to the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by rereading the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before and after sprinkling' means before and after the actual sprinkling, so the ברייתא never mentions time in the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Before and after' means before and after the meat became fit for sprinkling, which is exactly the split between no time and time in the day.

steps.title: Opening a new challenge from פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge. With פיגול, in both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, there was a מצוה to sprinkle the blood. The rest of the challenge continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a case where he made it פיגול, whether with קדשי קדשים or with קדשים קלים, there was a מצוה to sprinkle its blood,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against the idea that, for רבי שמעון, something that stands to be redeemed or sprinkled counts as if it already was. Only the opening of the case appears here, and the challenge is completed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings פיגול, an offering ruined by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten. Even there, there was a מצוה to sprinkle the blood once it was slaughtered. The question about how רבי שמעון rules in this case will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (opens a challenge)
An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten or burned
Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of lesser holiness

phrases.english: But isn't it so that if he rendered it piggul,
whether with offerings of the most sacred order
or with offerings of lesser sanctity,
there is a מצוה to sprinkle its blood,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא פִּיגֵּל, בֵּין בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים בֵּין בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, מִצְוָה לְמִיזְרְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 24 settles the wording question, a new challenge begins from the case of פיגול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of step 24 (built on step 17's principle) that, for רבי שמעון, meat whose blood stood to be sprinkled counts as having had a שעת הכושר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פיגול is a case where there was a מצוה to sprinkle the blood. The full challenge from this case is completed after this point.
